sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 152.9 ± 41.9 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry (L4) confirmed surface expression of myc-tagged GPR32 on whole blood and PBMC subsets. Direct functional impact of the tag on receptor signalling was NOT MEASURED in isolation; in vivo phenotypic studies of the transgenic model were performed but confounded by the whole-animal context.
sites.rationale: GPR32 is a GPCR with no signal peptide: the topology landmarks place residues 1–44 extracellular and residues 321–356 intracellular. Flow cytometry (L4) confirms the myc tag reaches the cell surface, ruling out the intracellular C-terminus and leaving the extracellular N-terminus as the sole terminal candidate. No ledger line names a specific residue, so the junction is topology-derived at position 0 (prepend before M1). Python confirmed residue 1 = M and TM1 begins at residue 45, giving 44 residues of extracellular space—well above the ≥3-residue minimum. Full-length human GPR32 with a myc reporter tag was cloned into a mammalian expression vector and expressed transgenically in mice (hGPR32myc × Fpr2−/− × Apoe−/− model). Flow cytometry on whole blood and PBMCs confirmed the myc tag is displayed on the cell surface.

sources.claim: ( D ) Flow cytometry histogram (representative of n = 3) showing GPR32 expression in naive whole blood from Fpr2 –/– ×Apoe –/– (dark gray) and hGPR32 Tg×Fpr2 –/– ×Apoe –/– (light blue) mice (left) and differential expression of hGPR32 in myc myc PBMC (purple) and neutrophil (dark blue) cell subsets (right).

literature_notes: All five ledger lines (L1–L5) derive from the same paper (PMC8670838) and describe the same myc-tagged full-length GPR32 construct. None names a specific insertion residue or loop. The C-terminus (residues 321–356) is intracellular per the topology landmarks and is excluded by the flow-cytometry surface-detection result (L4). No internal loop insertion is supported because no ledger line pins a residue or named loop for an internal site. The position is therefore topology-derived at the extracellular N-terminus (insert_after_residue = 0). Confidence is medium rather than high because the exact junction within the N-terminal region is not stated.
